verse: Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have. (Heb 13:5)

There is great gain in godliness combined with contentment; for we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it; but if we have food and clothing, we shall be content with these. (1 Tim 6:6-8)
Those who wish to get rich fall into temptation and get trapped in many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge them into ruin and destruction. (1 Tim 6:9)
Instruct those who are wealthy in this present age not to be haughty, nor to rely on the uncertainty of riches, but on God, who richly provides us with all things for our enjoyment. (1 Tim 6:17)
What do you have that you have not received? But if you have received it, why do you boast, as if you had not received it? (1 Cor 4:7)
No one is able to serve two masters. For either he will have hatred for the one, and love the other, or he will be devoted to one, and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth. (Matt 6:24)

Sell what you possess and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that will not wear out, a treasure that will not fall short, in heaven, where no thief approaches, and no moth corrupts. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. (Luk 12:33-34)

I have learned to be content in whatever circumstance I am. I know what it is to be poor, and I know what it is to have an abundance. In everything and all things I have learned the secret, both to be full and to be hungry, of living in abundance and of being in need. (Phil 4:11-12)
Whoever trusts in his riches will fall. But the just shall spring up like a green leaf. (Pro 11:28)
A good name is better than many riches. And good esteem is above silver and gold. (Pro 22:1)

Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth: where rust and moth destroy, and where thieves break in and steal. Instead, lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven: where neither rust nor moth destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. (Matt 6:19-21)

There is one who is enriched by spending sparingly, and this is his reward. He says: “I have found rest for myself, and now I alone will eat from my goods.” But he does not know how much time will pass before death approaches, and then he must leave everything behind to others and die. (Sir 11:18-19)
Like the partridge that hatches eggs which it did not lay, so are all who gather riches unjustly; in the middle of their life, it will abandon them, and in the end, they will be fools. (Jer 17:11)
He said to them: “Be cautious and guard yourself against all kinds of greed. For a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of the things that he possesses.” (Luk 12:15)
A greedy person stirs up conflict, but the one who trusts in the Lord will prosper. (Pro 28:25)

The crowd was questioning him, saying, “What then should we do?” But in response, he said to them: “Whoever has two coats, let him give to those who do not have. And whoever has food, let him act similarly.” (Luk 3:10-11)
Whoever is greedy for unjust gain disturbs his own house. (Pro 15:27)
Whoever gathers treasures by a lying tongue is vain and foolish. He will stumble into the snares of death. (Pro 21:6)
Whoever loves gold will not be justified. And whoever pursues wealth will be led astray by it. (Sir 31:5)
Do not rely on dishonest wealth. For these things will not benefit you in the day of disaster. (Sir 5:8)
A greedy man will not be satisfied with money. And whoever loves wealth will gain no profit from it. This too is vanity. (Eccl 5:10)

Wealth is not appropriate for a covetous man, and what use is money to a stingy person? He deprives himself only to amass wealth for others, and others will squander away his goods. He who is mean to himself, to whom will he be generous? He shall not take pleasure in his own riches. (Sir 14:3-5)
The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been so eager to be rich that they have wandered away from the faith and have pierced themselves with many sorrows. (1 Tim 6:10)

If a brother or sister is naked and daily in need of food, and if anyone of you were to say to them: “Go in peace, keep warm and nourished,” and yet not give them the things that are necessary for the body, of what benefit is this? (Jas 2:15-16)
Let the thief steal no more, but rather let him labor, working with his hands, doing what is good, so that he may have something to distribute to those who suffer need. (Eph 4:28)
When you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy anything from your neighbor, do not cheat one another. (Lev 25:14)

The soldiers also questioned him, saying, “And what should we do?” He said to them: “You should not exhort money from anyone by threats, and you should not make false accusations. Be content with your wages.” (Luk 3:14)
The eye of the covetous person is not content with his portion; he will not be satisfied till he withers his own soul. (Sir 14:9)
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence. (Matt 23:25)
Because of gain, many have sinned. And whoever seeks to be enriched, averts his eye. (Sir 27:1)
Remember that a greedy eye is evil. What has been made more greedy than the eye? Therefore, it sheds tears for any cause. (Sir 31:13)

Whoever receives a prophet, in the name of a prophet, shall receive the reward of a prophet. And whoever receives the just in the name of the just shall receive the reward of the just. And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones to drink because he is a disciple—amen, I say to you, he will not lose his reward. (Matt 10:41-42)

Render glory to God with a generous heart. And you should not reduce the first fruits of your hands. With every gift, have a cheerful countenance, and offer your tithes with gladness. Give to the Most High as he has given to you, generously, according to your means. For the Lord gives recompense, and he will repay you seven times as much. (Sir 35:10-13)

Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. And whoever sows generously will also reap generously. Each one giving, just as he has determined in his heart, neither out of sadness, nor out of compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver. (2 Cor 9:6-7)

Those who made sport of the birds in the sky, and those who stored up silver and gold in which people trust; there is no end to their attempts to get more. Those who schemed anxiously to get silver, there is no trace of their actions. They have all vanished and gone to their graves, and others have arisen in their place. (Bar 3:17-19)
Any one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple. (Luk 14:33)

He said: ‘This is what I will do. I will tear down my barns and build larger ones. And into these, I will gather all the things that have been grown for me, as well as my goods. And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods, stored up for many years. Relax, eat, drink, and be merry.’ But God said to him: ‘You fool, this very night your life is being demanded of you. To whom, then, will those things belong, which you have prepared?’ So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves and are not wealthy toward God.” (Luk 12:18-20)

Jesus said to him: “If you are willing to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and then you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” When the young man heard this word, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions. (Matt 19:21-22)

Amen, I say to you, it will be hard for a wealthy person to enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for the wealthy to enter into the kingdom of heaven. (Matt 19:23-24)
You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male or female servant, or ox, or donkey, or anything that belongs to him. (Exo 20:17)

Lay up your treasure according to the precepts of the Most High, and it will benefit you more than gold. Store up almsgiving in your treasuries, and it will obtain help for you against all evil. (Sir 29:11-12)

Blessed is he who shows concern toward the poor. The Lord will deliver him when the times are evil. The Lord will protect him and keep him alive and make him blessed in the land. You will not hand him over to the will of his adversaries. The Lord will sustain him on his sickbed. In his illness you will heal all his infirmities. (Ps 41:1-3)
Whoever possesses the goods of this world, and sees his brother to be in need, and yet closes his heart to him: in what way does the love of God abide in him? (1 Jn 3:17)
Do not neglect doing good and sharing what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God. (Heb 13:16)
Whoever blocks his ears to the outcry of the poor shall also cry out himself, and he will not be heard. (Pro 21:13)

Jesus, gazing at him, loved him, and he said to him: “You are lacking in one thing. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and then you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” (Mrk 10:21)

Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together and overflowing, will be placed on your lap. Certainly, the measure you give will be the measure you get back. (Luk 6:38)
Some distribute their goods freely, and they become wealthier. Others withhold unduly, and they are always in need. (Pro 11:24)
Whoever is merciful to the poor lends to the Lord. And he will repay him for his deeds. (Pro 19:17)

Give liberally and be ungrudging, so that the Lord your God may bless you, at all times and in all things to which you will put your hand. There will never cease to be poor people in the land; for this reason, I instruct you to open your hand to your poor brother, who lives among you in the land. (Deut 15:10-11)
